Keywords: minimal, swiss, grid, whitespace, typographic, editorial, clean, helvetica
Looks Like: Large type on a strict grid with wide margins and very little else. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and position, not from boxes or effects.
Use When: portfolio, architect, studio, editorial site, consultancy, documentation, photographer
Avoid When: Shops with many products, or brands that rely on warmth and chatter. Emptiness without strong type just looks unfinished.
Palette: One ink, one paper and one signal colour used sparingly: ink #111418, page #FFFFFF, signal #E4572E, rule #D9DCE1.
Type Approach: Neo-grotesque sans such as Inter Tight or Work Sans, with 2 or 3 sizes only. Set body at 17 to 18px with a 1.5 line height and left-align everything.
Layout: 12-column grid, generous outer margins, one idea per screen. Align everything to the grid and let blank space do the separating.
Motion: Almost none. Links change colour in 120ms ease-out and one page-load reveal of 300ms is the limit. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Centring everything; a thin sans at light weight on white; hiding the navigation to look clean; one huge image with no content
Accessibility: Thin grey text fails 1.4.3, so keep body at 4.5:1 or better. Keep visible focus rings (2.4.7) as the design has no boxes to fall back on. Check reflow at 320px (1.4.10).
Performance: low: text, a few images and no effects.
Checklist: Everything sits on the grid; Only 2 or 3 type sizes in use; Body text passes 4.5:1; Focus ring is visible on every link; One signal colour, used for one job

Keywords: neumorphism, soft, extruded, embossed, shadow, raised, pressed, monochrome
Looks Like: Controls that look pushed out of or pressed into a single-colour surface, made with one light and one dark shadow. Everything shares the background colour.
Use When: smart-home panel, music player, calculator, concept app, settings screen with few controls
Avoid When: Forms, shops, trades or anything people must read fast. The low contrast between a control and its surface is the problem, not a detail.
Palette: One mid-light surface with a lighter and a darker shadow of the same hue, plus one strong accent for state: surface #E3E8EF, highlight #FFFFFF, shade #B8C0CC, accent #1F5FBF.
Type Approach: A rounded, sturdy sans such as Nunito Sans or DM Sans at medium weight, 16px or larger. Use dark ink #1B2430 on the surface, never grey on grey.
Layout: Few, large controls with 24 to 32px gaps so shadows do not collide. One screen holds a handful of controls, not a dense form.
Motion: Press states move 100 to 150ms ease-out by swapping a raised shadow for an inset one. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Raised shadows on every element; grey text on grey surface; removing borders so fields are invisible; pastel everything
Accessibility: Weak edges fail 1.4.11 for controls and fields. Add a 1px border of #6B7686 or a clear fill state, and use a solid accent for the on or selected state. Never rely on shadow alone to show focus (2.4.7).
Performance: low: box-shadow only, no blur filters.
CSS Starter:
.control { background: #e3e8ef; border: 1px solid #6b7686; border-radius: 16px; box-shadow: 6px 6px 12px #b8c0cc, -6px -6px 12px #fff; }
.control:active { box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 8px #b8c0cc, inset -4px -4px 8px #fff; }
Checklist: Every control has a 3:1 edge or fill; Selected state uses colour, not only shadow; Text is dark on the surface; Focus ring is clear; Tested on a dim phone screen

Keywords: glass, frosted, blur, translucent, backdrop, layered, overlay, panel
Looks Like: Translucent panels that blur whatever sits behind them, with a thin light edge. Depth comes from the layer behind, so it needs a busy or colourful backdrop.
Use When: music app, weather app, system overlay, hero card over photo, dashboard widget, launch page
Avoid When: Text-heavy pages and trades or legal sites. Blur over changing content makes contrast unpredictable, and cheap phones struggle with it.
Palette: A photo or solid colour field behind, with white-tinted panels: backdrop #1D2B53, glass #FFFFFF at 16% alpha, edge #FFFFFF at 40% alpha, text #FFFFFF.
Type Approach: Clean sans such as Manrope or Outfit at 500 weight or heavier on glass, 16px minimum. Keep line length short as glass panels are small.
Layout: Few panels, 16 to 24px padding, stacked over a single backdrop. One layer of glass per screen, never glass on glass.
Motion: Panels slide or scale 200 to 300ms with ease-out. Do not animate blur radius. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Glass cards on a gradient blob; blur on every element; white text on a light photo; nested glass
Accessibility: Text over blur needs 4.5:1 against the worst part of the backdrop (1.4.3), so add a darker tint under the text. Offer a solid fallback for prefers-reduced-transparency and for browsers without backdrop-filter.
Performance: high: backdrop-filter repaints on scroll and costs on low-end phones; limit to 1 to 3 panels.
CSS Starter:
.glass { background: rgb(20 30 60 / 0.55); backdrop-filter: blur(14px); border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.4); border-radius: 18px; }
@supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) { .glass { background: #1d2b53; } }
Checklist: Contrast measured on the busiest part of the backdrop; Solid fallback exists; No more than 3 glass panels per screen; Tested on a mid-range phone; Blur is not animated

Keywords: brutalism, raw, bold, hard-shadow, thick-border, blocky, stark, loud
Looks Like: Hard edges, thick black borders, flat colour blocks and default-looking type pushed to extremes. Offset hard shadows and visible structure replace polish.
Use When: indie brand, creative studio, zine, music label, art gallery, youth product, event
Avoid When: Banks, clinics, law firms and anyone whose buyers want calm. The shout puts off cautious people.
Palette: Black outlines on flat, saturated blocks: ink #000000, paper #FFF8E7, hot #FF4D2E, block #FFD23F.
Type Approach: Heavy grotesque such as Archivo Black or Space Grotesk 700, plus a plain system serif or sans for body. Mix sizes hard, 14px to 120px.
Layout: Visible grid, 3 to 4px borders, boxes that touch or overlap. Dense in places and empty in others by choice.
Motion: Buttons jump 2 to 4px on hover with a 80ms linear shift of the hard shadow. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Pink and yellow with black outline on every card; random rotation of every box; giant type with no message behind it; hard shadows on everything
Accessibility: Strong borders help 1.4.11. Risk is clashing colours on text (1.4.3) and busy layouts that break reading order. Keep source order logical and focus rings thicker than the borders.
Performance: low: flat colour and borders with no heavy assets.
CSS Starter:
.btn { border: 3px solid #000; background: #ffd23f; box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #000; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; }
.btn:hover { transform: translate(2px, 2px); box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #000; }
Checklist: Reading order matches source order; Text passes 4.5:1 on every block; Not every box has a shadow; Focus ring beats the border weight; The shout fits the brand

Keywords: 3d, hyperreal, webgl, render, product, depth, model, spline
Looks Like: Lit 3D objects or photoreal renders that sit in the page and react to the pointer or scroll. The object is the main content.
Use When: product launch, hardware, car maker, jewellery, game, architecture visual, event
Avoid When: Content sites, trades and anything that must work on slow phones. A render that takes 6 seconds to appear loses the visit.
Palette: Neutral studio backdrop and one product colour: backdrop #0E1116, light #F2F4F7, product #3B82F6, shadow #05070A.
Type Approach: Clean geometric sans such as Sora or Plus Jakarta Sans, large and short. Keep copy to a headline and one line, as the model carries the page.
Layout: One hero scene, then ordinary sections below. Reserve the scene height so the page does not jump while it loads.
Motion: Slow orbit or rotate on scroll, 600 to 1200ms ease-in-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes. Show a still render.
Slop Habits: Floating blob shapes; a rotating cube with no purpose; stock 3D icons; heavy scroll-jacking
Accessibility: Canvas content needs a text alternative and keyboard route (2.1.1). Never trap scroll. Motion must stop or be removable (2.2.2) and respect reduced motion. Keep text off busy renders to pass 1.4.3.
Performance: high: 3D models, textures and WebGL cost bytes and GPU; ship a compressed model, lazy-load, and give a poster image.
Checklist: Poster image shown before and instead of 3D; Model under a stated byte budget; Text has a contrast backdrop; Page works with the canvas removed; Tested on a mid-range phone

Keywords: vibrant, blocks, colour-blocking, bold, saturated, playful, sections, flat
Looks Like: Full-width bands of saturated colour with big type and simple shapes. Each section has its own colour and one job.
Use When: startup landing page, kids brand, event, festival, food brand, campaign, product launch
Avoid When: Serious finance or medical sites, and any page where many colours would hide what to do next.
Palette: 3 to 4 saturated colours chosen as a set, not tints of one: blue #2446D8, yellow #FFC72C, coral #FF6B57, ink #14161A.
Type Approach: Bold sans such as Poppins or Bricolage Grotesque for headings with a calm sans for body. Check every text and block pair, not just the first.
Layout: Stacked full-width sections, 80 to 120px vertical padding, large simple shapes, 6 or 12 column grid. Give the main action the one loudest colour.
Motion: Blocks wipe or slide 250 to 400ms ease-out on first view only. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Every section a different random colour; confetti shapes everywhere; icons in coloured circles; yellow text on white
Accessibility: Colour pairs are the risk: yellow or coral text on white fails 1.4.3. Use ink on yellow and white on blue. Do not use colour alone to mean state (1.4.1).
Performance: low: flat colour and vector shapes.
Checklist: Each colour pair passes 4.5:1; One loudest colour for the main action; Colours chosen as one set; Meaning not carried by colour alone

Keywords: dark, oled, black, night, theme, low-light, battery, contrast
Looks Like: A near-black surface with light text and one or two bright accents. Depth comes from slightly lighter greys, not from shadows.
Use When: developer tool, media app, trading app, night-use app, music, camera, gaming
Avoid When: Print-like reading pages and older audiences in bright rooms, and any brand whose photos need white paper behind them.
Palette: Off-black base with stepped greys and one accent: base #0B0D10, raised #161A20, text #E8EAED, accent #5BC0BE.
Type Approach: Slightly larger and looser than light mode, since light-on-dark looks thinner. Try IBM Plex Sans or Inter at 400 or 500, 1.6 line height.
Layout: Separate layers by a grey step and a 1px edge of #262B33. Keep surfaces at 3 steps or fewer.
Motion: Fades of 150 to 200ms ease-out. Avoid bright flashes. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Pure #000000 with pure #FFFFFF text; neon accent on every item; a glow behind the hero; dark with grey text that fails contrast
Accessibility: Pure white on black can cause halation, so use #E8EAED. Muted grey text often fails 1.4.3; check at 4.5:1. Respect prefers-color-scheme and offer a switch.
Performance: low: plain CSS; OLED screens save power on dark pixels.
Checklist: Muted text passes 4.5:1; Text is off-white, not pure white; Layers separated by grey step; Light-mode option or preference honoured; Images checked on dark

Keywords: accessible, wcag, ethical, a11y, contrast, honest, plain, readable
Looks Like: Plain, high-contrast pages with obvious controls, large text and honest wording. Nothing hides, nags or tricks.
Use When: council, charity, school, health service, government, bank, any public site
Avoid When: Almost none; it fits every site. It is a weak choice only if used as an excuse for having no point of view.
Palette: Strong contrast and one clear action colour: ink #111418, page #FFFFFF, action #0B57D0, error #B3261E.
Type Approach: Readable sans such as Atkinson Hyperlegible or Public Sans at 18px or larger, 1.6 line height, left-aligned, 65 characters per line.
Layout: Single column for text, clear headings in order, big targets, forms with visible labels. Put the main action in plain view.
Motion: Minimal. State changes in 100ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Cookie banners that hide the refuse button; low-contrast grey help text; placeholder-only labels; countdown timers with no basis
Accessibility: Aim for 4.5:1 text (1.4.3), 3:1 for controls (1.4.11), visible focus not hidden by sticky bars (2.4.11), 24px minimum targets (2.5.8) and 44px in practice. Allow zoom to 200% and reflow at 320px (1.4.10).
Performance: low: light pages with few assets.
Checklist: Keyboard-only run of the main task; Zoom 200% and 320px width; Every field has a visible label; Errors say what to fix; Refuse is as easy as accept

Keywords: clay, soft, 3d, rounded, playful, inflated, pastel, friendly
Looks Like: Puffy, rounded shapes that look like moulded clay, with a soft inner highlight and a soft outer shadow. Colours are friendly and slightly saturated.
Use When: kids app, education, onboarding, game, wellness app, children's brand
Avoid When: Serious or dense tools, and trades. Chunky shapes waste space and look childish in the wrong place.
Palette: Mid-tone fills, not pastel-on-white: peach #F4A58A, sky #7CB8F2, mint #8DD6B4, ink #23283A.
Type Approach: Round, friendly sans such as Fredoka or Nunito at 600 weight for headings, with Nunito at 400 for body. Large sizes, short lines.
Layout: Big rounded cards, 28 to 40px radius, generous gaps. Few items per screen.
Motion: Bouncy press and hover 200 to 300ms with cubic-bezier(0.34 1.56 0.64 1). Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Every box inflated; pastel on white text; stock 3D character illustrations; three blobs in the background
Accessibility: Pastels give weak text contrast (1.4.3) so use dark ink on them. Inner shadows can blur edges, so give inputs a 3:1 outline (1.4.11).
Performance: low: shadows and gradients only; avoid blur filters.
CSS Starter: .clay { background: #f4a58a; color: #23283a; border-radius: 32px; box-shadow: 8px 8px 16px rgb(35 40 58 / 0.2), inset -6px -6px 10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), inset 6px 6px 10px rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5); }
Checklist: Dark ink on every pastel fill; Inputs have a clear outline; Not every element is puffy; Tested at 375px

Keywords: aurora, gradient, mesh, colour-flow, soft, ambient, background, vivid
Looks Like: Soft flowing colour fields behind the content, like light moving across sky. Use as a background only, with plain content on top. The house lint bans gradient heroes by default, so only use it when the brand asks for it.
Use When: music brand, creative tool, wellness app, event page, brand that already owns a colour flow
Avoid When: Trades, law, finance and any page that already looks generic. A gradient hero is the most copied look on the web.
Palette: Two or three related hues from the brand with a dark base: base #0F1220, teal #2BB3A3, green #7ED957, violet #6C5CE7.
Type Approach: A solid sans such as Space Grotesk or Figtree at 500 or higher, white or near-white on the dark base. Keep headings large and short.
Layout: Content in a clear column over one background field. Keep the field behind the first screen only, then drop to a flat base.
Motion: Background drifts very slowly, 20 to 40s linear, or stays still. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Purple-to-blue gradient; blurry blobs behind the hero; gradient text; same hero on every product page
Accessibility: Text over shifting colour fails 1.4.3 in places, so put text on a darker layer. Moving backgrounds need a pause or off (2.2.2). Use a still image for reduced motion.
Performance: medium: large blurred gradients repaint; use a pre-rendered image or a CSS gradient, not live blur.
CSS Starter:
.aurora { background: radial-gradient(60% 50% at 20% 20%, #2bb3a3 0%, transparent 70%), radial-gradient(50% 50% at 80% 10%, #6c5ce7 0%, transparent 70%), #0f1220; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .aurora { animation: none; } }
Checklist: Brand really owns this look; Text sits on a darker layer; Background is still under reduced motion; Gradient stops after the first screen; Passes 4.5:1 at the worst spot

Keywords: retro, futurism, synthwave, y2k, chrome, neon, 80s, space-age
Looks Like: The past's idea of the future: chrome type, grids, horizon lines, stars, scan lines and neon on dark. Nostalgic and theatrical.
Use When: game, music, event, film, arcade, tech brand with a retro story, merch
Avoid When: Trust-led sites, medical and finance. It also shows a lack of ideas if the brand has no link to the era.
Palette: Dark base with two hot colours and a chrome neutral: night #120B2E, magenta #FF2E93, cyan #19E3F5, chrome #D8DCE8.
Type Approach: A display face with character, such as Orbitron or Audiowide, for headlines only; set body in a plain sans like Rubik at 16px or larger.
Layout: Centred hero with a perspective grid, then ordinary sections. Keep body areas flat so text stays easy.
Motion: Slow grid scroll 8 to 12s linear loop, hover flicker 120ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Neon glow behind everything; purple-to-pink gradient sun; scan-lines over body text; monospace for ordinary copy
Accessibility: Neon on dark can be fine for contrast, but thin cyan text on purple fails often (1.4.3). Flicker and flash must stay under 3 per second (2.3.1). Stop looping motion on request (2.2.2).
Performance: medium: gradients and text-shadow are cheap, but large animated grids and filters are not.
CSS Starter:
.horizon { height: 40vh; background: linear-gradient(#ff2e93 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 100% 32px, #120b2e; transform: perspective(400px) rotateX(55deg); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .horizon { animation: none; } }
Checklist: Display font used for headlines only; Body text passes 4.5:1; Nothing flashes over 3 per second; Looping motion can be stopped; Link to the era is real

Keywords: flat, simple, vector, solid, icons, clean, colour, 2d
Looks Like: Solid colours, simple shapes, no gradients, bevels or shadows. The interface reads as paper cut-outs.
Use When: app, SaaS, small business site, information site, kiosk, dashboards
Avoid When: Complex tools where depth shows what is clickable. With no shadows, buttons can be mistaken for labels.
Palette: Solid colours from a small set: blue #1D6FE5, green #1FA463, sun #F5B700, ink #1A1F29, page #F7F8FA.
Type Approach: Plain sans such as Roboto or Source Sans 3 in 2 weights. Use size and colour for rank.
Layout: Clear card-free blocks on a 12-column grid, 8px spacing scale, one accent per screen.
Motion: Colour and position changes only, 150ms ease-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Same blue button on every page; icons in coloured circles; everything white with grey text; no sign of what can be pressed
Accessibility: Make controls obvious with a solid fill or underline (1.4.11). Do not use colour alone for state (1.4.1). Keep focus visible (2.4.7).
Performance: low: solid fills and vector icons.
CSS Starter:
.btn { background: #1d6fe5; color: #fff; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 12px 20px; }
.btn:hover { background: #1558b8; }
Checklist: Buttons look pressable; Focus ring visible; Spacing on an 8px scale; Colour not the only signal; One accent per screen

Keywords: skeuomorphic, texture, leather, wood, tactile, realistic, knobs, analogue
Looks Like: Interfaces that copy physical objects: leather, brushed metal, paper, dials and switches. Detail and shadows suggest touch.
Use When: music software, audio plugin, calculator, game, vintage brand, bakery, craft maker
Avoid When: Fast, text-heavy or mobile-first sites. Textures cost bytes and date quickly if the brand is not about craft.
Palette: Material tones with strong light: leather #5B3A29, brass #C9A24B, paper #F1E7D3, ink #1E1A16.
Type Approach: A slab or serif with some warmth, such as Roboto Slab or Lora, for headings; a plain sans for body text. Give text a dark fill on lighter textures.
Layout: Panels arranged like an object on a desk. Keep controls large and well separated.
Motion: Knobs and switches respond 120 to 200ms with ease-out; lids or pages flip 400ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Wood texture behind everything; fake stitching on every card; drop shadows on text; photos of objects with no relation to the work
Accessibility: Texture behind text lowers contrast (1.4.3), so put text on flat panels. Custom dials need keyboard and ARIA support (2.1.1, 4.1.2).
Performance: medium: textures and layered shadows add weight; use compressed images and CSS where possible.
CSS Starter: .switch { background: linear-gradient(#e0c06a, #a8832f); border: 1px solid #6b4f12; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25), inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5); }
Checklist: Text sits on a flat panel; Controls work by keyboard; Textures are compressed; Craft story is in the brand; Works at 375px

Keywords: liquid glass, refraction, translucent, fluid, ios, floating, controls, lensing
Looks Like: Floating controls and bars of clear material that bend and tint the content behind them. It is Apple's system look, built on glass, so it works best in native apps.
Use When: native iOS app, floating toolbar, media app, map overlay, concept site for an Apple-platform product
Avoid When: Ordinary websites and text-heavy pages. On the web it is a costly imitation and often illegible.
Palette: Let the content colour show through; keep a text-safe tint: tint #FFFFFF at 30% alpha, ink #0F1115, accent #0A84FF, shade #00000026.
Type Approach: System sans, in practice SF Pro on Apple or Inter as a web stand-in at 500 weight. Use short labels in controls.
Layout: Controls float over content with 12 to 20px inset, rounded ends, and few items. Keep the main text away from glass.
Motion: Controls morph 250 to 400ms with a spring-like ease. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Glass on every card; stacked glass on glass; blur with white text on white photos; copying iOS on a plain brochure site
Accessibility: Text on translucent material is the risk (1.4.3, 1.4.11). Add a stronger tint or a solid fallback for reduced transparency, as Apple's setting does.
Performance: high: refraction and backdrop blur repaint often; native does it well, the web does not.
CSS Starter: .float-bar { background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.6); border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.55); border-radius: 999px; padding: 8px 16px; }
Checklist: Solid fallback for no-blur and reduced transparency; Text passes 4.5:1 on busiest content; No glass on glass; Native app is the better home; Labels are short

Keywords: motion, animation, kinetic, scroll, story, parallax, transition, gsap
Looks Like: Movement carries the story: type that shifts, scenes that pin, transitions between pages. Content arrives in sequence with timing.
Use When: portfolio, agency, campaign page, product launch, film, award entry, museum
Avoid When: Trades, shops and people who want fast answers. Effects slow the task and hurt phones.
Palette: A restrained palette so the motion shows: ink #101114, paper #F5F3EE, accent #FF5A36, mid #8A8F98.
Type Approach: A strong display face such as Syne or Fraunces for headlines and a calm sans for body. Larger type reads better when it moves.
Layout: Pinned sections and long scroll but a clear skip link and simple fallback layout. One heavy effect per screen.
Motion: Entrances 400 to 800ms with cubic-bezier(0.22 1 0.36 1), page transitions 300ms, pinned scenes scrubbed by scroll. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes. Show the end state.
Slop Habits: Everything fades up on scroll the same way; parallax on every image; scroll-jacking; autoplay loops
Accessibility: Respect reduced motion (2.3.3 for motion from interaction), allow pause for anything over 5 seconds (2.2.2) and never hide content behind scroll triggers that fail without JS.
Performance: high: scroll-linked JS and large layers; animate transform and opacity only, and test on a mid-range phone.
Checklist: One heavy effect per screen; Content visible without JS; Reduced motion shows the end state; Tested on a mid-range phone; Motion has a purpose

Keywords: microinteraction, feedback, hover, toggle, loading, state, button, delight
Looks Like: Small, quick responses to actions: a button that presses, a toggle that slides, a field that confirms. Each one tells you the system heard you.
Use When: app, SaaS, forms, checkout, settings, any interface with actions
Avoid When: Pages with nothing to do. Adding motion where there is no action is just decoration.
Palette: Use your normal palette and add three state colours: success #1F8F55, error #C0392B, focus #0B57D0, ink #14161A.
Type Approach: No special type. Keep label text stable so buttons do not change width on state change; use tabular numbers for counters.
Layout: Same layout, with a space reserved for status messages so nothing jumps.
Motion: Press 80 to 120ms, toggle 150ms, success tick 250ms ease-out, never over 400ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes. Swap motion for a text or colour change.
Slop Habits: Confetti on every action; bouncing buttons; spinners on instant tasks; pulsing dots with nothing live
Accessibility: Status messages need a live region (4.1.3). Do not rely on colour alone (1.4.1). Keep targets 44px and focus visible (2.4.7).
Performance: low: transform and opacity transitions only.
Checklist: Every motion answers an action; Under 400ms; Status text announced to screen readers; Reduced-motion version works; Layout never jumps

Keywords: inclusive, universal, plain-language, cognitive, readable, multilingual, diverse, easy-read
Looks Like: Interfaces built for a wide range of people: plain words, clear steps, flexible text size and several ways to do the same thing. It is a way of working more than a look.
Use When: public service, health, education, charity, banking, housing, product for older users
Avoid When: Rarely wrong. It is incomplete if it is only a checklist and nobody from the audience has tested it.
Palette: Calm, high-contrast colours with meaning shown twice: ink #1A1D21, page #FBFBF8, link #0A5ABF, alert #A61B1B.
Type Approach: Highly legible sans such as Lexend or Atkinson Hyperlegible at 18px or more, with 1.6 line height and short lines. Avoid justified text.
Layout: One task per page where possible, numbered steps, labels above fields, plenty of space and an obvious back path.
Motion: Little. Never auto-play. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Using a stock photo of a diverse group; hiding help behind icons only; jargon in buttons; an overlay widget claiming to fix accessibility
Accessibility: Provide text alternatives (1.1.1), consistent help (3.2.6), redundant entry avoided (3.3.7) and accessible authentication (3.3.8). Allow text resize and spacing changes (1.4.12).
Performance: low: simple, text-first pages.
Checklist: Tested with people from the audience; Plain words in buttons; Text resizes to 200%; Steps are numbered; Help is in the same place on every page

Aliases: Invisible UI|Voice and Gesture UI|Screenless|Ambient UI
Keywords: zero ui, invisible, gesture, voice, ambient, predictive, minimal, automatic
Looks Like: Almost no visible controls: the product acts through voice, gesture, sensors or prediction, and the screen shows only what is needed now.
Use When: smart watch, voice assistant, in-car, wearable, smart home, camera app
Avoid When: Anything people must learn or check. Hidden controls are hard to find and hard to correct, so a screen needs a backup.
Palette: Plain, high-contrast screens with one signal: black #000000, white #F5F5F5, signal #3DDC84, warning #FFB300.
Type Approach: Very large, simple sans such as Inter or Roboto at 24px or more, one line of text per message, spoken or shown.
Layout: One action or fact per screen, centred, with a visible undo and a way to see what the system did.
Motion: Short confirmations 150 to 250ms ease-out, haptic or sound cues. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Hiding every control behind a gesture; assuming voice works for everyone; no way to undo; spying on behaviour to guess
Accessibility: Always give a visible, non-gesture route (2.5.1, 2.5.7) and captions for audio. Do not rely on voice alone. Let people see and undo what happened.
Performance: low: little is drawn, but sensors and models cost battery.
CSS Starter:
.glance { display: grid; place-items: center; min-height: 100dvh; background: #000; color: #f5f5f5; font-size: 1.5rem; }

Keywords: soft ui, evolution, gentle, rounded, subtle, shadow, modern, readable
Looks Like: The softer look of neumorphism with the fixes: gentle shadows, clear edges, stronger text and obvious states. Rounded and calm but readable.
Use When: wellness app, finance app, SaaS, settings, productivity tool, booking
Avoid When: Very dense tools and brutalist brands. It is mild and may feel bland without one strong accent.
Palette: Light neutrals with a clear accent: surface #F2F4F8, card #FFFFFF, edge #CBD2DC, accent #3D5AFE, ink #1B2230.
Type Approach: Friendly sans such as DM Sans or Figtree at 400 and 600. Body 16px and up, ink at least #1B2230.
Layout: Cards on a quiet surface, 12 to 16px radius, 16 and 24px spacing, one level of shadow.
Motion: Hover lift 150ms ease-out, press 100ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Soft grey shadows on everything; cards inside cards; pastel gradients; thin light text
Accessibility: Keep 1px edges so controls pass 1.4.11 and give selected states a solid colour. Text needs 4.5:1 (1.4.3).
Performance: low: simple shadows, no blur filters.
CSS Starter:
.card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #cbd2dc; border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgb(27 34 48 / 0.08); }
.card:hover { box-shadow: 0 4px 14px rgb(27 34 48 / 0.12); }
Checklist: Each control has a 3:1 edge; Only one shadow level; Selected states are solid; Body text passes 4.5:1; No cards inside cards

Keywords: dashboard, data, dense, analytics, table, chart, admin, monitoring
Looks Like: Compact tables, small charts and filters packed into a grid so an expert sees many numbers at once. Colour carries status and little else.
Use When: saas dashboard, admin panel, analytics, finance tool, operations, logistics, internal tool
Avoid When: Casual visitors and marketing pages. Density overwhelms people who are not trained on the data.
Palette: Neutral surfaces with a short status set: page #F4F5F7, panel #FFFFFF, ink #161A20, good #1F8F55, bad #C0392B, series #2F6FDB.
Type Approach: Compact sans with tabular numbers, such as Inter or IBM Plex Sans at 13 to 14px, and tabular-nums for every number column. Never go under 12px.
Layout: Fixed header and filter bar, 8px grid, 4 to 8px gaps, tables with sticky headers, charts aligned to a shared axis.
Motion: Almost none: 100ms hover and 200ms sort or filter fades. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: A dozen identical stat cards; rainbow charts; a donut for everything; fake numbers in mockups
Accessibility: Colour alone for status fails 1.4.1, so add icon or text. Keep chart contrast at 3:1 (1.4.11), offer a data table for each chart, and keep targets at least 24px (2.5.8).
Performance: medium: large tables and many charts; virtualise rows and load charts as needed.
Checklist: Numbers align right in tabular figures; Status uses text or icon as well as colour; Every chart has a table view; Rows at least 24px tall; Real data used in the mockup

Aliases: Trades Clear|Call and Quote|Plain Local|Phone-First Local
Keywords: plumber, electrician, builder, roofer, local, trades, call, quote, phone, service
Looks Like: A plain page that says who you are, where you work and how to ring, within the first screen. Big phone button, short quote form and proof from real jobs.
Use When: plumber, electrician, roofer, builder, locksmith, cleaner, driving instructor, garage
Avoid When: Fashion, art and brands that sell a mood. It is for people who need a job done soon, not for browsing.
Palette: Strong, trusted and plain: ink #14213D, page #FFFFFF, action #0B7A3B, warning band #FFD60A, rule #D5DAE1.
Type Approach: Sturdy sans such as Source Sans 3 or Public Sans at 18px, headings at 700. Phone number set large with tabular figures.
Layout: One column on mobile with a sticky call bar; services list, area, three real job photos, reviews from the owner's records and a short quote form. Phone number in the header and footer.
Motion: Almost none. Buttons change in 120ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Stock photos of smiling workers; three icon cards for services; a hero video; invented review counts and awards
Accessibility: Tap-to-call as a real tel: link, 48px targets (2.5.8), labels on every field, contrast 4.5:1 (1.4.3) and visible focus (2.4.7). Say prices and hours in text.
Performance: low: text, a few compressed photos and no video.
CSS Starter:
.call-bar { position: sticky; bottom: 0; display: flex; gap: 8px; padding: 8px; background: #14213d; }
.call-bar a { flex: 1; min-height: 48px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #0b7a3b; color: #fff; font-weight: 700; }
Checklist: Phone number visible without scrolling; tel: link works on a phone; Area and hours stated; Photos are the owner's own jobs; Reviews and numbers come from the owner; Quote form has 4 fields or fewer

Aliases: Local Warm|Cafe and Shop Warm|Independent Warm|Friendly Local
Keywords: cafe, shop, salon, bakery, independent, warm, people, photo, neighbourhood, friendly
Looks Like: A friendly page led by large photos of the place, the people and the products. Opening hours, address and menu are easy to find, and the tone is welcoming.
Use When: cafe, bakery, salon, barber, florist, independent shop, bookshop, deli
Avoid When: Law, finance and technical products. It is also weak if the business has no good photos of its own.
Palette: Warm, specific colours taken from the shop's own things: ink #2B2118, page #FBF6EE, brand #B5452B, leaf #5F7F4E. Do not default to cream with clay; pick from real signage or packaging.
Type Approach: A friendly serif or soft sans chosen for the brand, such as Fraunces or Bitter for headings, with Nunito Sans for body at 17px. Do not use one family at one weight.
Layout: Big photo first, then hours and address, menu or services, a short story and a map. Photo-led but clear, with irregular, not identical, blocks.
Motion: Light: one soft hero move of 500ms and 200ms hover states. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop the movement and keep only instant state changes.
Slop Habits: Stock photos of coffee and laptops; a hero with cream and terracotta by default; a pill badge above the headline; a script font for everything
Accessibility: Menu as real text, not a photo (1.1.1, 1.4.5). Alt text for photos that matter, contrast 4.5:1 over images (1.4.3), 48px targets and hours stated in text.
Performance: medium: photo-heavy, so use responsive sizes, WebP or AVIF, width and height set, and lazy loading below the fold.
Checklist: Photos are of the real place and people; Hours and address visible on first screen; Menu is text, not an image; Colours taken from the shop's own things; Images have width and height set
